coverage_of_risk.rationale: No tests exist anywhere in app/, and the untested code is precisely the risky logic: data transformation, filtering, sorting, pagination, and URL state. The pure functions in format.ts are the cheapest tests this PR could have shipped and didn't.

evidence: app/package.json:6-10 — no test script, no runner, no test files in the app
behaviour_not_implementation.rationale: There are no tests to evaluate on this axis; the app asserts nothing about its own behaviour.

regression_power.rationale: Once the acceptance suite stops guarding this app, breaking any of the covered-by-spec behaviours — alternate-form exclusion, page clamping, slot ordering — fails no test, because there are none.

evidence: app/ — no test files at all (measured tests.files = 0)
signal_to_noise.rationale: No tests means no noise, per the rubric's 'no tests: 3'; there is also nothing earning its keep.

findings.issue: Pure, user-visible helpers (humanize, dexNumber 4-digit padding, latestFlavorText last-English-entry + whitespace collapse, orMissing) have no unit tests despite being the cheapest coverage in the repo
findings.suggestion: Add vitest unit tests for format.ts as a starting point; these are pure functions with spec-pinned outputs

findings.issue: pokemonCards' id >= 10000 alternate-form cutoff, dedup, and dex-number sort are unguarded; a refactor could silently reintroduce Mega forms into every type/move/ability list
findings.suggestion: Unit-test pokemonCards against fixture refs including an id-10003 form, a duplicate, and unordered ids

findings.issue: Combined q/type/generation filtering, param validation, and page clamping (page=0/abc/999) are untested
findings.suggestion: Call the exported loader directly with Request objects for edge URLs; assert count, page, totalPages, and card ids

findings.issue: getIndex's speciesTypes slot ordering and EXCLUDED_TYPES filter drive every type badge and the /types list; untested
findings.suggestion: Test getIndex against a stubbed fetch covering excluded types and multi-slot pokemon

findings.issue: Densest transform in the app — default game (last by version-group order), method grouping/ordering, level-up sorting — has no coverage
findings.suggestion: Loader unit test with a small fixture pokemon asserting game default, method order, and level ordering

findings.issue: Client-side sort's nulls-last-in-both-directions invariant and direction toggle are regression-prone and untested
findings.suggestion: Render MoveTable with createRoutesStub (current React Router testing guide) and assert ordering with null power/accuracy cells

findings.issue: Pre-hydration input recovery, 150ms debounce, and back/forward control-sync effects are subtle client logic with no tests
findings.suggestion: Component tests via createRoutesStub covering typed-before-hydration input, navigation, and URL-sync of selects

findings.issue: Response cache: rejected-promise eviction, 60s TTL, and 404-to-null mapping are untested; a refactor could cache failures or serve stale data past the live-data-overlay scenario
findings.suggestion: Unit-test cached()/api with a controllable fake fetch: rejection eviction, expiry, 404 -> null, apiOr404 throwing a 404 data response

findings.issue: ErrorBoundary's 404-vs-500 branch and the splat not-found route are untested error paths
findings.suggestion: Component test rendering the boundary with isRouteErrorResponse-shaped and unknown errors

findings.issue: No test script or test runner dependency, so any future tests have no CI entry point
findings.suggestion: Add vitest (or node:test) and a 'test' script wired to the repo's npm test flow where possible

summary: The agent shipped zero tests of its own — no runner, no script, no files — leaving the app's riskiest logic (alternate-form exclusion, type-slot assembly, filter/pagination clamping, move-table derivation, and the pure format helpers) entirely dependent on the acceptance suite. The code is well factored for testing: pure functions in lib/, plain exported loaders, and React Router v8's createRoutesStub for components, so coverage would have been cheap. Once the harness suite is gone, almost any regression in data handling would ship silently.
